overview: Studenica linked dynastic memory, religious institutions, stonework and painting in medieval Serbia.

items.text: Stefan Nemanja founded Studenica in the late twelfth century. Members of the ruling family were buried there.
The complex included monastic facilities within an enclosing wall, with associated churches and hermitages outside it.
Nearby quarries and a workers' settlement supplied and shaped marble for the Church of the Virgin.
Its architecture combined Romanesque and Byzantine forms. King Milutin's church of 1314 brought another generation of commissioned painting to the site.
